item.title: Auro Metals Q2 FY26 net loss widens to CAD 567,549
item.description: Auro Metals posted a net loss of CAD 567,549 for the three months ended June 30, widening from CAD 236,338 a year earlier. Loss per share from continuing op
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Auro Metals posted a net loss of CAD 567,549 for the three months ended June 30, widening from CAD 236,338 a year earlier. Loss per share from continuing operations widened to CAD 0.0055 from CAD 0.0028; discontinued-operations loss was nil versus CAD 47,553. Cash climbed to CAD 13.41 million at June 30 from CAD 85,378 at Dec. 31, 2025, while total assets rose to CAD 50.96 million. Mineral property interests surged to CAD 36.51 million from CAD 4.09 million, reflecting the Santa Barbara project acquisition completed May 13. Total liabilities jumped to CAD 15.69 million from CAD 2.35 million, including CAD 12.87 million in deferred anniversary payments recorded as other payables. item.title: Gold Terra posts near-breakeven Q2 loss as flow-through premium reversal offsets higher marketing costs
item.description: Gold Terra posted a comprehensive loss of CAD 726,239 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, slightly narrower than CAD 762,507 a year earlier. Operating e
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Gold Terra posted a comprehensive loss of CAD 726,239 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, slightly narrower than CAD 762,507 a year earlier. Operating expenses rose to CAD 1.8 million from CAD 1.09 million, led by higher marketing-related costs, stock-based compensation, travel, professional fees. Flow-through share premium reversal increased to CAD 1.54 million from CAD 532,095, offsetting much of the higher spending. Exploration spending totaled CAD 5.67 million, mainly on the Con Mine option area at CAD 3.63 million. Cash fell to CAD 247,393 from CAD 7.56 million at year-end, leaving working capital of CAD 245,651. item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: TriMas lifted its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to USD 1.6-1.7, up from USD 1.5-1.7. Forecast calls for 3%-6% sales growth, based on FY 2025 net sales of USD 645.7 million. Adjusted operating profit margin expected to improve by more than 300 bps from FY 2025’s 5.3%. Assumptions include interest income of USD 9-10 million per quarter in Q3 and Q4, interest expense of USD 18-20 million. Outlook follows Q2 net sales of USD 171.8 million, operating profit of USD 14.9 million, EPS of USD 0.52. item.title: Stewards says USD 20 million Hawthorne property deal faces dispute over USD 1 million deposit
item.description: Stewards agreed to buy The Hawthorne property in Chatham, Massachusetts for USD 20 million cash, with a USD 1 million deposit in escrow. Seller issued an Au
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Stewards agreed to buy The Hawthorne property in Chatham, Massachusetts for USD 20 million cash, with a USD 1 million deposit in escrow. Seller issued an Aug. 18 default notice, citing a missed Aug. 10 closing date, seeking to keep the deposit as liquidated damages. Stewards disputes the default claim, instructed the escrow agent to hold the deposit, with recovery likely to hinge on court action. Transaction completion is uncertain, with potential liquidity impact if the deposit is impaired or written off. item.dc:creator: MT newswire
item.content:encoded: 03:39 PM EDT, 08/25/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Financial stocks were slightly higher in late Tuesday afternoon trading, with the NYSE Financial Index up 0.3% and the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) adding 0.2%. The Philadelphia Housing Index increased 0.1%, and the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) advanced 0.2%. Bitcoin (BTC-USD) was shedding 0.2% to $78,859, and the yield for 10-year US Treasuries dropped 6.5 basis points to 4.639%. In corporate news, UBS (UBS) is expanding its efforts to offer customers deposits with Middle East lenders to take advantage of higher regional savings rates, Bloomberg reported. UBS shares rose 1%.

item.content:encoded: Flowers Foods held its Q2 2026 results Q&A, attended by CEO A. Ryals McMullian, CFO D. Anthony Scaglione, and IR head JT Rieck. Management flagged a challenging fresh packaged bread category, citing budget pressure, shifting preferences, and sustained competitive activity. Back-half improvement expected from new business wins, incremental cost-savings actions, and innovation to address portfolio gaps. Guidance implied Q3 year-over-year sales declines, followed by Q4 stabilization as new wins ramp, pricing laps, and Nature’s Own marketing gains traction. Inflation outlook: 2026 commodities largely hedged; exposure remains in oil, diesel, and packaging resin; fiscal 2027 planning underway. item.title: Forge Resources intersects visible gold at Alotta project in Yukon
item.description: Forge Resources completed 2026 diamond drilling at the Alotta Project in Yukon’s Dawson Range Gold Belt, totaling 2,792 m across six holes. Visible gold wa
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Forge Resources completed 2026 diamond drilling at the Alotta Project in Yukon’s Dawson Range Gold Belt, totaling 2,792 m across six holes. Visible gold was intersected at the Payoff Zone in hole ALT-26-020 within a 1 cm quartz vein at 217 m depth. A 651 m deep hole at the Commission Zone cut continuous porphyry-style alteration, ending in strong stockwork veining with molybdenite-bearing mineralization. Drilling has ended for the season; assays from ALS Laboratories are pending and expected to be released following QA/QC review.
